decisions.reason: As a peripheral sports-system line with higher support complexity and no later visible reinforcement, its option value is likely now outweighed by the benefit of reallocating resources to the firm's more core, trend-led flooring business.

A mobile arena floor is a specialized and likely costlier option to keep open, and after several years the firm would probably abandon it if it has not clearly proven strong demand or strategic importance.

Because it overlaps with another mobile arena floor line and sits outside the firm's main interior-focused growth direction, management would be inclined to prune it once uncertainty has had time to resolve.
This flagship chevron parquet line fits the firm's core capabilities and stated strategic direction toward style-oriented natural aesthetics, so its upside still justifies continued commitment.
The squash-court finish is a narrow niche complement whose value depends on the sports segment, making it a likely candidate for exit when the firm refocuses its portfolio.
Although cheap to carry as an accessory, this sports-floor skirting line has limited standalone strategic value and is more likely to be removed if related sports products are not priorities.
